pr_title: pcrlock: support measurement of big files
pr_body:
Introduces a new read flag in fileio to read large files, and pcrlock uses it for locking raw files and initrd.

Fixes #31883
pr_comments: Completely foregoing the size check seems a bit too much, how about adding a version of the helper that takes in a custom max size? And then specify something like 1G that should be enough in normal cases?

> Completely foregoing the size check seems a bit too much, how about adding a version of the helper that takes in a custom max size? And then specify something like 1G that should be enough in normal cases?

Yes, this makes more sense.

On one side I can simply change  `READ_FULL_BYTES_MAX` into something line  `(1U * U64_GB - UINT64_C(1))` and that will be all. This will change the global limit for every `read_full_xxx` family calls. Is this OK?

The other alternative is still add a new flag, something line `READ_FULL_FILE_LARGE_FILE` that will change the limit of 64MB to 1GB if the flag is set, and enable this flag in the pcrlock verbs. This will not change the default limit of 64MB, except when the flag is set.

What option does makes more sense for you?
Second one please, as we want the existing limit for other cases

> Second one please, as we want the existing limit for other cases

Yes, of course. Should be done

The file doesn't need to be loaded into memory at once. IMO the correct solution is to have `make_pcrlock_record` accept a stream and use `EVP_DigestInit` + `EVP_DigestUpdate` + `EVP_DigestFinal` on the data stream.

> The file doesn't need to be loaded into memory at once. IMO the correct solution is to have `make_pcrlock_record` accept a stream and use `EVP_DigestInit` + `EVP_DigestUpdate` + `EVP_DigestFinal` on the data stream.

That is what is suggested here: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/31889#discussion_r1536617197

But make_pcrlock_record cannot be replaced, there is use case where the parameter needs to be a place in memory. I proposed to create a variant of it that accept a fd. If this is accepted I will go for it.

Yeah, just turn this into a loop. Reading massive blobs into memory as one is always going to be inefficient.

Just read 64K or so at once. That should be sufficeint.
@keszybz  I changed the implementation, reading now 64k blocks to calculate the hash.
lgtm, just two minor tweaks please

issue_context.title: pcrlock lock-raw and lock-kernel-initrd fails with long files (>64MB)
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

256

### Used distribution

all

### Linux kernel version used

all

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-pcrlock

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

```sh
$ systemd-pcrlock lock-raw --pcr=9 /boot/efi/opensuse-microos/6.7.9-1-default/initrd

Failed to read data from stdin: Argument list too long
```
